Hafley spent Saturday reviewing tape from the 20-7 loss - pleased with how the starters, led by Malik Willis, executed together, but flagged backup-QB depth and offensive-line protection as the real items to fix before the next test. No game this weekend; next joint practices are Aug. 20 against the Giants ahead of an Aug. 22 preseason game.

Rookie WR Chris Bell (recovering from a torn ACL) was activated off the physically-unable-to-perform list; OT Austin Jackson is fully cleared from his toe injury. Miami held a Member Day practice today closed to the public; the next public milestone is Wednesday's joint practice with the Giants ahead of an Aug. 22 preseason game.

Giants and Dolphins staffs set "rules of engagement" (protect QBs, no blindside hits, front-up thuds only) ahead of today's joint practice, two days before Saturday's Aug. 22 preseason game. Hafley on rookie WR Chris Bell's ACL recovery: "I think he's in a really good place right now... he's accelerating, decelerating, able to cut" - hopeful to get him into a preseason game before Week 1. OT Austin Jackson is fully cleared from his toe injury; OL Jamaree Salyer, TE Greg Dulcich, TE Ben Sims, S Dante Trader Jr., and WR Kevin Coleman remain day-to-day.

New York's defensive front dominated Thursday's joint practice at Miami's facility, with tempers flaring repeatedly; Giants rookie OT Francis Mauigoa (ex-Hurricane) left with a stinger (not considered serious) and starting RT Jermaine Eluemunor also exited early, but no major new Dolphins injury emerged from the session. Coach Jeff Hafley confirmed rookie WR Chris Bell, activated off the non-football-injury list Monday, will not play in Saturday's preseason game against the Giants: "there's still a lot of steps to go" in his ACL recovery.

Miami hosts the Giants today at 4pm at Hard Rock Stadium in the second preseason game of Hafley's tenure, after Thursday's joint practice turned openly hostile — RT Austin Jackson was ejected for throwing a punch (he returned for the final 11-on-11 period) and Giants LB Abdul Carter took a swing at LT Patrick Paul after losing a rep; Hafley said postgame he'd be disappointed to see more fighting and that it isn't a sign of toughness. Rookie WR Chris Bell, activated off the non-football-injury list last week, will not play today — Hafley called him week-to-week in his ACL recovery, with hope he's ready for the regular season. DT Zach Sieler is expected to be ready for the opener; DT Kenneth Grant is week-to-week and sitting out the rest of this week.

The Giants routed Miami 26-3 Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium — Jameis Winston threw for 150 yards and ran for a touchdown in the first half. Chris Bell (ACL) did not play, still week-to-week per Hafley.

In the days after Saturday's 26-3 loss to the Giants, Hafley confirmed linebacker Trey Moore (ankle, hurt vs. the Giants) is sidelined with a quick return unlikely, as Miami works through the roster decisions that must be finalized by Sunday, Aug. 30's 53-man deadline.

Hafley confirmed Trey Moore will need surgery on the ankle injury from the Giants game -- a longer-term absence than Tuesday's 'unlikely to return quickly' framing suggested. Miami is expected to place him on injured reserve by roster-cutdown weekend, using one of its two IR-return designations ahead of Sunday, Aug. 30's deadline. Separately, Miami claimed WR Ryan Miller off waivers from the Giants and waived WR Tahj Washington to make room.

Clarified: Trey Moore can't go on injured reserve until Miami's initial 53-man roster is set, so the team is carrying him as one of its 90 for now; Miami is expected to place him on IR around Aug. 30-31, once cuts are final, preserving his eligibility to return later this season.

Miami began its round of roster cuts Sunday, waiving 12 players -- including CB Alex Austin, RB Coleman Bennett, and linebackers Stephen Dix Jr. and Jaheim Thomas -- as all NFL teams face today's 6pm ET deadline to reach 53. Trey Moore's IR placement is still expected to follow immediately after the initial 53 is set.

Miami's initial 53 is set: the QB room turned over completely at the deadline -- Quinn Ewers traded to Jacksonville Saturday, then Kyle McCord acquired from Green Bay Sunday for the identical 2028 sixth-round pick Miami got for Ewers, a direct swap. Malik Willis is the Week 1 starter with McCord now the backup.

First-round DT Kenneth Grant went on injured reserve with a designation to return, for a leg injury -- out a minimum of four games, eligible back as early as Week 5; Hafley had called the roster "thin still" beforehand. Trey Moore's expected ankle-surgery IR placement was finalized alongside it. For the record: Miami's actual Week 1 opener is Sunday, September 13 at the Las Vegas Raiders (4:25pm ET, FOX) -- not September 4, which is the Hurricanes' season opener at Stanford, a different team entirely.

During the same roster-cut weekend that set Miami's 53, the Dolphins traded Quinn Ewers, waived Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski, and acquired backup QB Kyle McCord from Green Bay -- the moves that actually cleared the room to make Malik Willis the unambiguous starter.

Head coach Jeff Hafley named six team captains ahead of Sunday's opener at Las Vegas, including QB Malik Willis -- Hafley said the vote reflects the locker room's respect for Willis rather than the honor simply following the starting job.

Hafley said all 53 active-roster players practiced Wednesday -- tight end Will Kacmarek and linebacker Ronnie Harrison Jr. returned after missing last week, and receiver Chris Bell (off the non-football-injury list) is a full go for Week 1. Receiver Tyreek Hill will not play Week 1, with doctors reportedly recommending he wait until at least October to attempt a comeback. Malik Willis makes his first career start as a Dolphin Sunday at Las Vegas.

Coach Jeff Hafley said all 53 active roster players practiced Wednesday and Thursday ahead of Sunday's 1pm opener at Las Vegas, with only minor limitations (Ronnie Harrison Jr., Will Kacmarek). The Raiders will be without star tight end Brock Bowers (knee) for the game. Malik Willis makes his first career start at quarterback for Miami; Tyreek Hill remains out.

Friday's final injury report before Sunday's 1:25pm PT opener at Las Vegas lists only Will Kacmarek (calf) and Ronnie Harrison Jr. (hamstring) as limited, with Seydou Traore a full participant; the Raiders remain without tight end Brock Bowers (knee). Malik Willis makes his first career start Sunday.

Season opener day: kickoff at Allegiant Stadium is 1:25pm PT / 4:25pm ET, with Las Vegas installed as a 3.5-point favorite (total 40.5). Malik Willis makes his first career start; the Raiders open a new era under head coach Klint Kubiak and veteran QB Kirk Cousins.

Season opener result: Raiders beat Dolphins 27-13 at Allegiant Stadium, never trailing. Willis passed for 220 yards with an interception and ran for a 14-yard touchdown but was sacked five times; Cousins threw three touchdown passes.
Miami's Week 2 opponent is confirmed: at the San Francisco 49ers, Sunday, September 20, at Levi's Stadium, a fast West Coast trip after Sunday's 27-13 opening loss at Las Vegas.

Ahead of Sunday's game at San Francisco (4:25pm ET, Fox), Miami is a roughly 13 to 13.5-point underdog. Rookie safety Kyle Louis is out with an MCL sprain from the opener, long snapper Tucker Addington is dealing with a shoulder injury, and quarterback Malik Willis -- starting since the Vegas opener -- has a toe injury but returned to full practice Wednesday and is expected to play.

threads.title: Miami Hurricanes fall camp and the Mensah era
threads.current_state: No. 5 Miami (2-0) is a 20.5-point favorite at Wake Forest tonight (7:30pm ET, ESPN). Four players are out per the ACC's official availability report: CBs Frederique Jr. and Lucas, DB Antoine, and TE Luka Gilbert (out for the season, newly reported). Miami hasn't forced a takeaway through two games; Cristobal says his real concern is complacency, not Wake Forest's talent, after two blowout wins over Stanford and Florida A&M.

timeline.summary: First tracked: fall camp opens, Cristobal sets a deliberately measured tone ('no time or room to overpraise anyone') after last season's title-game loss, Duke transfer Darian Mensah installed as starting QB following Cam Ward and Carson Beck as Miami's third straight top transfer-portal arm.

Camp's second week has shifted focus to offensive- and defensive-line rotation battles as position groups sort out; the secondary, which returns the most production of any unit from last year's title-game run, remains the roster's most settled group. Several outlets project Miami to win the ACC and contend for another national title, but Cristobal's measured opening-week tone continues to set the pace.
Fall camp held its first scrimmage Friday evening at Hard Rock Stadium; Cristobal said afterward he was happy with the team's progress, continuing his deliberately measured tone from camp's opening.

Cristobal confirmed Monday, on The Joe Rose Show, that transfer WR Cam Vaughn has been dismissed from the team - the fourth camp departure this preseason, after safety Conrad Hussey, CB Jontavius Wyman, and edge Hayden Lowe. No official reason was given; Vaughn was arrested in Georgia in July on a reckless-driving charge. Darian Mensah remains the starting quarterback.

Miami holds its second fall-camp scrimmage today at Hard Rock Stadium, following an Aug. 14 scrimmage where Cristobal praised the team's explosive plays and said it emerged relatively clean on the injury front. Depth-chart projections confirm Duke transfer Darian Mensah as the unambiguous starting QB, with redshirt freshman Luke Nickel backing him up - Miami's third straight year starting a transfer-portal QB. No further roster departures have surfaced since Monday's Cam Vaughn dismissal.

Friday's second scrimmage at Hard Rock Stadium was a closer back-and-forth than the first — the offense reportedly had the better of the work this time, a reversal from scrimmage one, where the defense had the upper hand. Cristobal called it good, competitive work with two weeks left before the Sept. 4 opener at Stanford.

Cristobal confirmed sophomore tight end Luka Gilbert (6-7, 255) will miss the entire 2026 season after injuring himself at home over the summer -- 'he is going to miss the season and he will be back the following year.' Gilbert played 68 snaps as a true freshman in 2025 and was in the mix to back up Elija Lofton; the news comes alongside confirmation that Hayden Lowe and Jontavius Wyman are no longer with the team, with nine days left before the Sept. 4 opener at Stanford.

Two legal situations now shadow fall camp days before kickoff. WR Cam Vaughn, dismissed August 17 after a reckless-driving arrest in Georgia (96 mph in a 55 zone), has sued the university and the NCAA seeking transfer-portal entry, which Miami has declined to facilitate. Separately, RB Jordan Lyle -- one of camp's more impressive players -- faces a felony fleeing/eluding charge plus a reckless-driving misdemeanor from a July 10 incident in Broward County; Cristobal hasn't dismissed him, saying the program is letting the legal process play out. The season opens Friday, September 4 at 9pm ET at Stanford, on ESPN.

Kickoff details for Friday's real season opener are set: 9pm ET at Stanford Stadium on ESPN, headlined by a halftime performance from Bay Area rapper E-40, with Miami entering ranked No. 7 nationally off last year's national title-game run -- a rematch of last year's 42-7 Miami win over the Cardinal. Neither Cam Vaughn's lawsuit against UM and the NCAA nor Jordan Lyle's felony fleeing/eluding charge has moved since Monday's reporting.

Cam Vaughn's lawsuit against UM and the NCAA has been dropped -- both sides parted ways after Miami submitted a legislative relief waiver request allowing him to re-enter the transfer portal, resolving the one legal cloud that had a clean resolution available. Jordan Lyle's felony fleeing/eluding charge remains open and unaddressed, with the program continuing to let the legal process play out; he remains on the roster. Friday's opener at Stanford is now one day out.

Miami opened the season with a 45-6 rout of Stanford at Stanford Stadium. Darian Mensah went 27-of-30 for 400 yards and five touchdowns; Malachi Toney set the program's single-game receiving record with 233 yards on 12 catches, three for touchdowns. Jordan Lyle's felony charge remains the one open legal thread.
Miami's home opener is set for Thursday, September 10 at 8pm against Florida A&M at Hard Rock Stadium -- the last non-conference tune-up before ACC play begins.

Ahead of tonight's home opener against Florida A&M, Miami's secondary is thinner than it was at Stanford: corner OJ Frederique Jr. suffered a serious shoulder injury on his first defensive snap of the season and will be out for an extended stretch, corner Ja'Boree Antoine is also out, and safety Dylan Day is sidelined by a non-football illness. Cristobal declined to give a hard update on running back Jordan Lyle's status.

No. 7 Miami routed Florida A&M 77-7 Thursday night at Hard Rock Stadium to move to 2-0, behind quarterback Darian Mensah and receiver Malachi Toney. FAMU's starting quarterback is reportedly out for the season with a thumb injury. Corner OJ Frederique Jr. remains out for Miami with the shoulder injury sustained in the opener.

Friday's Wake Forest test now has a number: Miami (2-0, No. 5) opened as a 23.5-point favorite over a Wake Forest team that's also 2-0 after beating Akron 38-16. Kickoff 7:30pm ET, September 18, in Winston-Salem.

Cristobal confirmed junior cornerback Xavier Lucas will also be out roughly a month, joining Frederique Jr. and Ja'Boree Antoine on the sideline; junior safety Dylan Day, previously out, is expected back for Friday's game at Wake Forest.

Friday's game at Wake Forest (7:30pm ET, ESPN) is set with Miami favored by roughly 20.5-23.5 points; the Hurricanes are missing three regular cornerbacks (Frederique Jr., Antoine, and now Lucas, out ~a month) and rank 125th nationally in turnover margin (-3), numbers that haven't mattered yet against lighter competition.

Miami's ACC availability report confirms four players out for tonight's Wake Forest game: cornerbacks O.J. Frederique Jr. (shoulder) and Xavier Lucas (roughly a month), defensive back Ja'Boree Antoine (hasn't played this season), and tight end Luka Gilbert, out for the season with a pre-fall-camp injury not previously reported. The spread has settled at Miami -20.5, O/U 56.5, after drifting from an earlier -22.5. Cristobal's stated worry isn't Wake Forest's talent -- he called them 'a very mature team' with 17 of 22 starters as upperclassmen -- it's his own team's complacency after two blowout wins. Miami still hasn't forced a takeaway through two games.

threads.current_state: Genghis Cohen (LA import) is confirmed for Sunset Harbour, winter 2026, no exact date. La Sponda opens Saturday September 19 at Vita at Grove Isle in Coconut Grove -- the most concretely dated opening this season. Royale Pizza Napoletana targets October on Lincoln Road; La Pecora Bianca targets this fall at Merrick Park.

Several openings confirmed live, including China Grill's actual location.
Manoli opens; fall 2026 anticipated list published.
Stephen Starr's Slim's opens at Bal Harbour Shops in the former Makoto space, one of several July arrivals across Brickell, Coconut Grove, and Coral Gables.
Crisppi's opens a second location in West Miami; Flight West opens in South Miami pairing live-fire cooking with an ambitious whiskey program.
Both openings get their first dedicated edition coverage, including the detail that Crisppi's second location took over a former Pollo Tropical drive-thru on SW Eighth Street.
Miami Spice's discounted dining season opens citywide, running through September 30 with $40 lunch/brunch and $50-65 dinner prix-fixe menus.

August roundup adds Burgers & Shakes (North Miami), LandShark Bar & Grill at Dolphin Mall, Star Burger, and a reopened Stormy Monday; Miami Slice's Coconut Grove opening slips to late August/early September.
Night Owl Cookies (West Kendall) and Pura Vida (Kendall) join the summer opening wave.

Correcting last week's timeline: Miami Slice's Coconut Grove location actually opened Aug. 12, not late August as previously reported, with an expanded dine-in menu, slice-bar seating, and wood-fired items exclusive to the Grove spot.

New to the summer wave: Star Burger (a grass-fed concept from the family behind Estrella Insurance), LandShark Bar & Grill by Margaritaville at Dolphin Mall, Takay (a 10-seat, 17-course Japanese omakase on Coral Way), and 1986 Steak House (an Argentine concept in Coconut Grove from Grupo Orfano); Stormy Monday, previously slated to close, reopened with a refreshed menu instead.

Burgers & Shakes opened in North Miami and Miami Slice's Coconut Grove location is targeting a late-August/early-September debut - the latest additions to the summer wave. Miami Spice discounted dining continues through Sept. 30.

Burgers & Shakes opened a second South Florida location Aug. 4 inside the historic 1954 General Tire Building in the MiMo Historic District — designed by architect Robert Law Weed, most recently home to Andiamo Brick Oven Pizza, which closed after 23 years. Separately, Medium Cool, the jazz lounge beneath the Gale Hotel on Collins Avenue, plays its final night tonight after nearly four years, with nightly live jazz through 10pm; the team says it's searching for a new Miami home rather than closing for good.

Medium Cool's Yelp listing now shows a new address — 1690 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, a few blocks from its old Gale Hotel home — with hours Wed-Sun 7pm-3am (4am Fri/Sat), suggesting the jazz lounge didn't stay dark long after Saturday's farewell night. Not yet confirmed by press coverage.

The Estrella Insurance family opened Star Burger at 4901 SW 8th St. on Tamiami Trail -- smashburgers, chili fries, a Miami Hurricanes-branded burger (Estrella is the Canes' official burger sponsor this year) -- and Stormy Monday reversed an earlier planned closure to reopen with a refreshed menu instead. Burgers & Shakes' MiMo/North Miami location and Miami Slice's Coconut Grove opening remain in progress; Miami Spice discounted dining continues through Sept. 30.

Star Burger, from the family behind Estrella Insurance, is open on Tamiami Trail; Stormy Monday completed its reprieved reopening with a refreshed menu. Correction on location: Burgers & Shakes' new spot is in North Miami, not MiMo as earlier reported. Miami Slice's Coconut Grove debut remains pending, not yet confirmed open.

Attention shifts from confirmed August openings to Miami New Times' fall preview: Genghis Cohen (the real "Seinfeld" restaurant, opening in Miami Beach this winter in the former Sardinia space in Sunset Harbour), Royale Pizza Napoletana, La Sponda, and La Pecora Bianca -- none with confirmed dates yet beyond "this fall" or "winter."

Genghis Cohen's Miami arrival firms up: the 42-year-old LA restaurant that inspired Seinfeld's "The Chinese Restaurant" episode confirmed for 1801 Purdy Ave in Sunset Harbour, its first location outside California, opening winter 2026.

La Sponda, Gioia Hospitality's waterfront Italian restaurant at Vita at Grove Isle in Coconut Grove, opens Saturday September 19 for dinner service Wednesday through Sunday, with full lunch, brunch, and seven-night dinner service expanding in November. threads.title: Miami Freedom Park Civic Center
threads.current_state: Miami's commission voted Thursday to keep City Hall at the Pan Am terminal in Coconut Grove rather than relocating to Freedom Park -- resolving one concrete piece of the broader civic debate over the future of that waterfront property.

timeline.summary: First tracked: civic center topped off, full project scope confirmed.

With Freedom Park's new eight-story City of Miami Administration Building on track, the question of what happens to the current City Hall -- a 1934 Pan Am seaplane terminal on prime Dinner Key bayfront, listed on the National Register of Historic Places -- is now openly on the table. Officials say no decision is final ('all really premature'), but commissioners are expected to weigh options once the new building opens in about two years.

The Miami city commission voted Thursday to keep the historic Pan Am terminal at Dinner Key in Coconut Grove as the city's primary City Hall, rather than relocating city government operations to the Miami Freedom Park development.

threads.title: 2026 CRE capital markets under pressure
threads.current_state: The institutional buying wave now runs six deep in roughly three weeks: Ares ($108.7M, Hialeah/Sweetwater warehouses), Midtown Capital ($86M, Doral industrial), Dalfen ($21.3M, Doral warehouse via Terreno Realty), Phoenix Realty Group ($64.8M, Altavista Bay Pointe apartments), and Longpoint Partners' $195M purchase of a 10-building, 730,000-square-foot small-bay industrial portfolio -- still the largest single deal of the wave.

timeline.summary: First tracked: CBRE Q2 update shows deal volume down 24% YoY, construction spending below plan, hiring slowing.
South Florida-specific data surfaces: commercial sales volume down 13% year over year to $5.42B in H1 2026.
Waste Management pays $379M for 146 acres in Medley to build a landfill; $366M of the price, 96%, is seller financing rather than a bank loan.

A LoopNet analysis of roughly 5,000 office listings finds Miami's average asking rent, $59.66/sq ft, now the highest in the US, ahead of New York's $50.56 - a sign of how much capital has relocated to Miami since 2020 even as deal volume overall stays soft.

Pebb Capital buys a Miami Beach office building with $69M in ACORE Capital financing; a Wynwood commercial parcel sells for $24.5M, the region's priciest trade that week - real transactions behind the aggregate rent data.
Rents in Miami's top towers cross $200/sqft for the first time, anchored by Peter Thiel's family office paying a record $250/sqft at 830 Brickell; Q2 leasing citywide up nearly 45% YoY to 1.3M sq ft.
Citywide full-service asking rent hits an all-time high of $63.63/sqft (+2.0% QoQ, +6.3% YoY), with 429,712 sqft of positive Q2 absorption.

A separate Commercial Observer analysis puts Miami's average asking rent at $67.12/sqft, up 7% year over year, with availability down to 14.9% from 17.1% - an independent data set reinforcing the same trend TenantBase reported yesterday.

A third independent report, from Commercial Property Executive, confirms the same trend: Miami Class A rent up 6% YoY to $80.85/sqft, vacancy down 40bp to 14.4%; The Real Deal confirms Miami now has the highest average office asking rent in the US.

No new office-market report this week beyond Tuesday's Commercial Property Executive figures; South Florida's routine deal flow continues - an $8.4M Lantana assisted-living sale, a $6.8M Lauderhill shopping center, and a $23M Doral parcel anchored by a used-car dealership.

Robert Rivani's RIVANI closes on 404 Washington Avenue, a South of Fifth office/retail building, for $31.5M ($200.95/sf), financed with a $29.5M BridgeInvest loan - the latest single-transaction data point in the same record-office-rent story.

A new MIAMI Realtors/RWorld report formally ranks South Florida the No. 1 office market in the US, with average asking rents up 7.1% year over year to roughly $61/sq ft citywide - the aggregate confirmation of the trend three separate reports had already flagged.

Harbor Group International pays $109M for the 505-unit Emerald Palms apartment complex near Zoo Miami; a Fisher Island condo at 7811 Fisher Island Drive sells for $15M to software executive Mark Sutcliffe - more individual deal flow landing behind Friday's No. 1 ranking.

A CRE Daily/Largo Capital update shows Miami leading every major US market in same-asset office rent growth (4.0% YoY), Brickell Tier I space above $130/sqft, and a 2026-27 construction pipeline tracking to just 1.6% inventory growth - the slowest pace in a decade.

The Real Deal reports South Florida i-sales up 19% YoY, YTD volume over $9B, led by industrial activity; a separate office-only subset (~90 deals, $1.3B) was down 11.5% YoY, cap rates 7.12%-8.39% - a more uneven picture than the rent-growth headlines alone suggested.

Largo Capital's August Florida market update adds context to Tuesday's i-sales story: private investors now account for over half of South Florida CRE buyers versus roughly 19% institutional, industrial vacancy runs 7.0-7.2% with rents near peak ($16.42-$17.26 NNN), and CMBS conduit execution has stretched beyond typical timelines as spreads widen. No new headline transaction; consistent with, not a reversal of, Tuesday's uneven-recovery read.

South Florida was formally ranked the No. 1 office market in the US this week (Miami Realtors/RWorld, published Aug. 7): lowest vacancy and fastest rent growth among the top 25 US markets, Miami asking rents up 7.1% YoY to $61/sqft, Fort Lauderdale up 16.4% to $43.50/sqft, West Palm Beach-Boca up 21.2% to $49.90/sqft - all far outpacing the national average of +2.4% to $33.60/sqft. Deal flow continued at the individual-transaction level: Ken Griffin's Citadel sold its Palm Beach office building at 125 Worth Ave for $86M to Blackstone's Revantage (he paid $83M in 2023); Harbor Group paid $109M for the 505-unit Emerald Palms apartment complex; Moishe Mana's Mana Common paid $20.3M for a former post office building at 100 NE First Ave.

A Commercial Property Executive analysis found Miami office investment-sales volume has fallen sharply this year - just $387.2M year-to-date through August - even as roughly 4.4M sq ft remains under construction through 2028, a reminder that the record-rent, No.-1-market headlines coexist with a much quieter transaction market. The Real Deal's latest weekly deal digest topped out with a $140M Delray Beach senior-living sale (a PGIM Real Estate affiliate to Artemis Real Estate Partners).

Individual development activity continues even as aggregate sales volume stays thin: Miami's newest residential tower is nearing sellout at roughly 80% sold to buyers from more than 30 countries; the Bird Road District development secured $84.5M in financing; Walmart bought 24 acres in Westlake. A reminder that record rents, quiet transaction volume, and continued new construction are all simultaneously true of this market.

Two more individual Miami deals closed: an El-Ad National Properties affiliate paid $62.3M ($778.75/sq ft) for the 80,000-sq-ft office building "The Grove at 3250 Mary" in Coconut Grove, and a venture of Miami Design District Associates and Raycliff Capital lined up $125M in construction financing for the Sweetbird North office/retail project.

A separate trade topped this week's South Florida deal sheet: Ilya Karpov sold a vacant waterfront lot at 2740 North Bay Road, Miami Beach, for $72M - more than tripling the $20.8M he paid in 2022 - brokered off-market by One Sotheby's. A Capital Realty Services affiliate also sold a 31,000-sq-ft mixed-use building at 1200 Washington Avenue for $10M.

This week's South Florida deal sheet (The Real Deal, published Aug. 21) adds a 155,000-sq-ft industrial building at 11900-11905 SW 128th St, sold for $24.5 million, and a new-construction, 10,500-sq-ft waterfront mansion at 270 South Hibiscus Drive, Miami Beach, which sold for $50 million — both landing on top of last week's North Bay Road and 1200 Washington Avenue trades.

This week's deal sheet adds a smaller, steadier trade: a 10,300-sq-ft industrial building at 6400 NW 84th Ave sold for $6.5M to an affiliate of Roberts Oxygen Company, a modest counterpoint to the larger waterfront and industrial deals of the past two weeks.

The week's headline trade: SJC Ventures sold the newly built, Whole Foods-anchored Doral Marketplace (8.2 acres; 38,000-sq-ft Whole Foods plus 40,700 sq ft of strip retail including J.Crew, Shake Shack, and First Watch) for $83M to a group led by Jonathan Perlman, who assumed $50.1M of existing debt -- the largest South Florida deal sheet entry in weeks, a step up from the prior two weeks' smaller industrial trades.

Cortland Partners sold the 812-unit Portofino Place Apartments in West Palm Beach for $208 million ($256,200/unit) to a venture tied to FRH Realty and Fairfield Residential -- more than double last week's $83M Doral Marketplace sale and the largest South Florida deal in over a month.

Midtown Capital Partners bought a 14-property, roughly 300,000-square-foot industrial portfolio in Doral for $86 million ($296/sf), acquiring from 13 sellers tied to the Waas family, who had developed and held most of the properties for decades. The deal is being framed around rising demand from local businesses for smaller industrial bays.

Ares Management paid $108.71 million for two Miami-area warehouses totaling 372,619 square feet (~$292/sq ft) -- a third institutional buyer in about a week, alongside Rockpoint's Apollo-financed 12-story acquisition, Midtown Capital's $86M Doral industrial portfolio, and the $208M Portofino Place apartment sale.

The Real Deal's daily sheet shows continued but smaller-ticket South Florida trades: Baptist Health paid $53.5M for a 92,700 sq ft Coconut Creek retail building (~$577/sq ft, from Kohl's), and an Emerald Group entity paid $27.6M for a Lake Worth Beach nursing home. Neither rivals the institutional industrial/multifamily deals of the prior two weeks.

Dalfen Industrial paid $21.3 million ($239/sq ft) for an 89,000-sq-ft Doral warehouse leased to AerSale, buying from a Terreno Realty affiliate that had held it since 2012 -- a third institutional industrial buyer in the market in under two weeks, alongside Ares' $108.7M Hialeah/Sweetwater purchase and Midtown Capital's Doral portfolio.

A New York-based entity linked to Phoenix Realty Group paid $64.8 million for the 269-unit Altavista Bay Pointe apartments in Miami, bought from 184 Holdings LLC -- a fourth institutional buyer in three weeks alongside Ares, Midtown Capital, and Dalfen. Separately, year-to-date private-label CMBS and CRE CLO issuance nationally reached $39.7 billion through June, tracking near a record pace, with bank lending up roughly 80% and private credit up roughly 133% year over year -- more competitive financing options for 2026 refinancings even as office loan maturities remain the market's weak link.

Boston-based Longpoint Partners paid $195 million ($267/sf) for a 10-building, 730,000-square-foot Miami-Dade small-bay industrial portfolio, 90% leased across 74 tenants averaging roughly 10,000 square feet each -- the fifth institutional Miami-area deal in three weeks and the largest single transaction of the wave.
Dalfen Industrial added a sixth deal to the wave, paying $21.3M for a fully leased Airport West/Doral warehouse (7600 NW 26th St) bought from Terreno Realty, per a September 15 announcement.

threads.title: Miami Marine Stadium's restoration referendum
threads.current_state: Resolved: Miami voters approved Referendum #172 with more than 68% support, clearing the way for a 40-year Global Spectrum/Oak View Group and Breakwater Hospitality management deal to restore and reopen Marine Stadium.

timeline.summary: First tracked: City Commission approved the Global Spectrum/Oak View management deal in February; referendum set for August 18; partial restoration already underway.

Additional detail surfaces: the deal is formally Referendum #172, with early voting set for August 3-16 and a specified revenue split (93% events, 85% sponsorship) plus a separate $65-85M restoration bond beyond the initial $10M.
Early voting confirmed to begin tomorrow, August 3; the adjacent Seaquarium site's marina redevelopment surfaces as a related but separate decision over the same stretch of public waterfront.
Early voting opens as scheduled, running through August 16 ahead of the August 18 vote.

Gloria Estefan and Savannah Buffett (Jimmy Buffett's daughter) publicly voice support for restoration; the National Trust for Historic Preservation is campaigning ahead of the Aug 18 vote. Early voting continues through Aug 16.
Early voting enters its final two days, through Aug 16, ahead of the Aug 18 vote; no new endorsements or opposition reported since Wednesday.

Early voting closes tomorrow, Sunday, August 16 - three days ahead of the August 18 vote. No new endorsements or organized opposition surfaced this week beyond the National Trust for Historic Preservation's active campaign and Wednesday's public support from Gloria Estefan and Savannah Buffett.

Early voting closes today as scheduled, three days ahead of Tuesday's Aug. 18 vote. The Associated Press ran a national feature today revisiting the stadium's history - its 1963 opening, its closure after Hurricane Andrew in 1992, and Jimmy Buffett's own letter urging its preservation before his 2023 death. No new endorsements or organized opposition surfaced this week.
Early voting is closed; the vote itself is tomorrow, Tuesday. No new organized opposition or endorsements surfaced over the weekend. Results are expected Wednesday.

Voting is underway today on Referendum #172; the measure needs a simple majority to pass. The Miami Herald editorial board endorsed a 'yes' vote this week, calling it possibly the last realistic chance to save the building; the Brickell Homeowners Association remains the most organized opposition, citing noise and traffic from large-scale events. No results are in yet - they're expected Wednesday.

Miami voters approved Referendum #172 with more than 68% in favor, clearing the way for Global Spectrum L.P. (Oak View Group) and Breakwater Hospitality Group to restore and manage Marine Stadium for up to 40 years. The measure needed only a simple majority; it passed by a wide margin.

threads.title: Miami Seaquarium's marina redevelopment
threads.current_state: Terra Group/David Martin's roughly $100M vision for the shuttered Seaquarium site now includes a fully accredited aquarium with no marine mammals, a research and education center, and a public baywalk alongside the previously reported 325-slip marina and 500-boat dry stack. County estimates put the project's value to Miami-Dade near $750M over the life of the lease; final County Commission approval is still pending, with environmental regulators flagging wetlands and coral concerns.

timeline.summary: First tracked: marina application details surface - 325 slips, 500-boat dry stack, fuel depot; environmental review pending; potential late-2026 groundbreaking.

Additional scope surfaces: a fully accredited, no-marine-mammal aquarium, a research/education center, and a public baywalk; county estimates the project's value to Miami-Dade at close to $750M over the life of the lease. County Commission approval still pending.

threads.current_state: Giannis skipped Greece's FIBA World Cup qualifiers this week to join an informal, players-organized minicamp with Klay Thompson, Bam Adebayo, and the rest of Miami's retooled roster (Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr.) -- early, voluntary work ahead of official training camp, which opens September 29 at Kaseya Center before the preseason opener October 3 in Quebec City.

timeline.summary: Klay Thompson reached a buyout agreement with the Dallas Mavericks Aug. 21 and, per ESPN's Shams Charania, intends to sign with Miami once he clears waivers on a two-year, ~$13M deal with a player option in year two. Giannis Antetokounmpo skipped Greece's FIBA World Cup qualifiers to join an informal, players-organized minicamp this week with Klay Thompson, Bam Adebayo, and other new pieces (Bobby Portis, Tim Hardaway Jr.) ahead of official training camp, which opens September 29 at Kaseya Center.

timeline.summary: Brad Marchand confirmed on social media he had a 'last-minute' offseason surgery on a hip/sports-hernia injury he played through in 2025-26, including the February Olympics; recovery could keep him out for the Sept. 29 opener. Home opener is Oct. 10 vs. Minnesota at Amerant Bank Arena.

Recovery estimate sharpens from 'two or more months' to a concrete range: six to ten missed games, with an earliest possible return around mid-October — still addressing the hip and sports-hernia issue Marchand played through all of 2025-26, including the February Olympics.

Florida's preseason and regular-season schedules are official: a four-game preseason opens September 20 at home against Carolina, with games September 22 at Raleigh and September 24 and 26 against Tampa Bay; the regular season opens September 29 at Carolina.

Florida announced its four-game preseason schedule: home to Carolina September 20, at Carolina September 22, at Tampa Bay September 24, home to Tampa Bay September 26. FanDuel installed the Panthers as the odds-on favorite to win the 2027 Stanley Cup at +650. The regular season opens September 29 at Carolina, the newly crowned 2026 champion.

Barkov gives his own camp-eve comments, "really excited" after full recovery from last year's knee injury and a gold-medal Worlds run captaining Finland.
Training camp opened today at Fort Lauderdale's Baptist Health IcePlex with Markstrom/Schmid already set in net and Barkov fully healthy; a public Fan Fest follows Saturday, September 19.

Camp opened Thursday at Baptist Health IcePlex with Barkov looking fully recovered and Brady Tkachuk skating as a Panther for the first time since June's trade. threads.title: Miami-Dade's "Vice City" pitch to Rockstar Games
threads.current_state: Miami's downtown GTA6 banner ordinance and Miami Beach's separate branding deal both stand as approved. Since then, county-level officials -- the Miami-Dade police chiefs association, the sheriff, and at least one commissioner -- have publicly objected to any county use of the branding, citing the game's violence, even as a 'Welcome to VI' sign reportedly goes up near the Kaseya Center. The city has embraced the branding; the county wants no part of it.

timeline.summary: Wider reporting confirms Miami-Dade's June 29 pitch to Rockstar Games for a county-wide Vice City marketing takeover -- MIA airport, PortMiami, Metromover, and Tropical Park -- as a potential new county revenue stream tied to the GTA 6 launch. Nothing formally approved.

Grand Theft Auto VI is now confirmed for a worldwide launch on November 19, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S, giving Miami-Dade's pitch to Rockstar an actual deadline to move on before. County officials reiterate nothing has been formally agreed to or approved, and any deal would still need to clear standard county review.

A city-level ordinance from Commissioner Damian Pardo -- allowing up to six paid downtown banners at $202,000 each (Oct 15-Dec 31), with proceeds funding the Underdeck Heritage Trail park after a $60M federal grant for it was pulled -- goes to a Miami city commission vote today. Miami-Dade's sheriff and a county commissioner oppose it; the county's chief judge and clerk of courts want courthouses excluded from any branding. Distinct from the still-unapproved county-level Vice City pitch deck.

Miami Beach's city commission voted 4-3 to approve its own, separate marketing arrangement with Rockstar -- restricted to the terms "VI" and "Vice City" on private beach equipment like chairs and umbrellas, running October 15 through December 31 -- after real debate over the game's violent content. The City of Miami's downtown banner ordinance (Commissioner Pardo's plan for up to six paid banners at $202,000 each) was separately on Thursday's commission agenda; its specific vote outcome could not be independently confirmed from available reporting as of this morning, which conflated it with the Miami Beach vote in several outlets.

Miami Beach's approved deal is now specified as a roughly $3 million marketing agreement with Rockstar for discreet 'VI'/'Vice City' branding on Boucher Brothers beach chairs and umbrellas, Oct 15-Dec 31. Two days after Thursday's scheduled vote, no outlet has yet reported a recorded result for the City of Miami's separate downtown banner ordinance (Commissioner Pardo's plan, $208,000 per banner, proceeds to the Underdeck park) -- an unusually long reporting gap for a local commission vote.

A giant 'Welcome Back to Vice City' sign is being installed on the Kaseya Center roof under a separate ~$4 million deal among Rockstar/Take-Two, Miami-Dade County, and the Heat's arena affiliate. The City of Miami's downtown ordinance now has specific public terms ($208,000 per banner, funding the Underdeck park project), though its own commission vote outcome remains unconfirmed.

The downtown banner ordinance's sponsor (Commissioner Damian Pardo), exact operating window (Oct 15-Dec 31, bracketing GTA6's Nov 19 launch), and a hard cap (six banners citywide, 56 total days) all became public. The commission's own legislative file still shows no recorded vote, over a week past its scheduled hearing.

Reporting surfacing Wednesday evening confirms Miami's city commission approved the downtown banner ordinance 4-3 -- the vote yesterday's edition flagged as still outstanding. Terms are unchanged from what was already public. The same day, Miami Beach's commission separately approved a $3 million Rockstar marketing deal, 4-3, for beach-chair and umbrella branding.

New pushback since the ordinance passed: the Miami-Dade Association of Chiefs of Police, at least one county commissioner, and the county sheriff have publicly objected to any county-level use of GTA6 branding, citing the game's violent content -- a distinctly county-level objection that doesn't touch the city's own downtown-banner ordinance or Miami Beach's separate beach-branding deal. Separately, a large 'Welcome to VI' Vice City sign is reportedly going up near the Kaseya Center as part of Rockstar's roughly $3M marketing arrangement, with a broader campaign expected around October 10.
